outcome.description: completed means authoring and review are finished: CI guardrails pass and should-change tests fail before fix deployment or pass afterward. failed means unexpected results need correction; needs_human means an unresolved operator or product question.

human_questions.description: Questions that prevent this lane from completing. Empty when outcome is completed. Squadron decides who receives them and where work resumes.

linked_sql_pr.description: The txc-sqlserver-database PR this locks in.

authority.description: Where the expected value comes from. Only these two authorities can be asserted; a value derived from the code under test asserts the bug.

citation.description: The comment/author or the published bulletin/rate table.

unwritten.description: Scenarios deliberately not written, each with its reason: 'needs authority' (no authority established the expected value — pair it with an entry in open_questions) or 'covered by the A/B' (a V1 path, config-only behavior, or anything the endpoint cannot observe). The second is a decision, not a gap.

authority_conflicts.description: Where SME statement and state-published material disagree — escalate, never pick.

open_questions.description: Questions a human must answer, each actionable on its own: the scenario, the exact figure needed, and the authority that would supply it. 'Needs confirmation' cannot be resumed by the next run.

validation.description: Automatic staging CI results assessed against fix deployment state. Before deployment, should-change failures are expected; afterward those tests pass. Guardrails pass throughout.

result_reference.description: CI run or report supporting the observed results; empty until available.
